scope: Proposition 8.6 (Compact-profile estimate) of the manuscript “Pure-Point Spectrum for the Two-Dimensional Anderson Model at Every Positive Disorder” (preprints/Pure-Point-Spectrum-for-the-Two-Dimensional-Anderson-Model-at-Every-Positive-Disorder-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 261 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 17487e3a2720b36f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 54-55. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let φ : R2 → Rq be compactly supported and Lipschitz, piecewise smooth with bounded gradients and piecewise regular interfaces. Let its center c be prescribed from the offset and external independent randomness. At full stage n, lim sup R→∞, τ→0 bN /R→∞ E Qstart φ((· − c)/R)  ≤ Cdn Z R2 |∇φ|2 dx, (8.18) where C is absolute. Here n and the profile are fixed; the thresholds may depend arbitrarily on them. The estimate is uniform over the allowed masks and centers, and remains valid with the expectation conditioned on the offset. 54 More generally, let f be supported in a square of side at most AR whose position is prescribed from the offset and external independent randomness, and suppose that f has global Lipschitz constant at most B/R. Then E Qstart(f) ≤ CA,B(dn + o(1)) (8.19) in the same fixed-n regime, uniformly over all such data and prescriptions. Thus each assertion holds to any fixed additive tolerance for all sufficiently large spatial and torus scales and all sufficiently small τ; no rate uniform in n is asserted.
